paper_title: Adapting General-Purpose Embedding Models to Private Datasets Using   Keyword-based Retrieval
caption: Retrieval performance of MAP@10 for different m and sampling strategies.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The bar chart illustrates the retrieval performance, measured by MAP@10, for two different sampling strategies, Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy and Uniform Sampling Strategy, across various values of 'm'. The horizontal axis represents the values of 'm', ranging from 6 to 10, while the vertical axis represents the MAP@10 values, ranging from 23.0 to 27.0. The Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy is depicted by purple bars, and the Uniform Sampling Strategy is represented by yellow bars. The purple bars are grouped together on the left side of the chart, corresponding to 'm' values from 6 to 10, with values of 26.0, 26.8, 26.4, 26.6, and 26.6, respectively. The yellow bars are grouped together on the right side, corresponding to the same 'm' values, with values of 24.5, 24.7, 25.6, 25.1, and 24.5, respectively. The chart allows for a visual comparison of the performance of the two sampling strategies across different 'm' values, with the Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy consistently showing higher MAP@10 values than the Uniform Sampling Strategy.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the retrieval performance, measured by MAP@10, for different values of 'm' and two sampling strategies: Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy and Uniform Sampling Strategy. The horizontal axis represents the values of 'm', ranging from 6 to 10 in integer steps, and is labeled as 'm'. The vertical axis is labeled as 'MAP@10' and has a linear scale, ranging from 23.0 to 27.0 with a tick label interval of 0.5. The chart displays grouped bars, with the Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy represented by purple bars and the Uniform Sampling Strategy represented by yellow bars. For the Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy, the bars have approximate MAP@10 values of 26.0, 26.7, 26.4, 26.6, and 26.5 for 'm' values 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10, respectively. For the Uniform Sampling Strategy, the bars have approximate MAP@10 values of 24.4, 24.7, 25.6, 24.9, and 24.4 for 'm' values 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10, respectively. The bars are grouped by 'm' value, with the two sampling strategies presented side by side for each value. The bars are not sorted in a specific order, and no bars are visually emphasized.
model_annotations.German: This diagram represents the retrieval performance of MAP@10 for different values of 'm' and compares two sampling strategies: Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy and Uniform Sampling Strategy. The x-axis contains the categories, labeled 'm', with values ranging from 6 to 10 in ascending order. The y-axis represents the MAP@10 values, ranging from 23.0 to 27.0, with a linear scale and tick labels at intervals of 0.5. The diagram displays two groups of bars, each representing a sampling strategy, with the Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy in purple and the Uniform Sampling Strategy in yellow. For the Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy, the bars have approximate MAP@10 values of 26.0, 26.7, 26.3, 26.6, and 26.5 for 'm' values 6 through 10, respectively. For the Uniform Sampling Strategy, the bars have approximate MAP@10 values of 24.5, 24.8, 25.6, 25.1, and 24.5 for 'm' values 6 through 10, respectively. The bars are grouped by 'm' value, with the purple bar appearing first, followed by the yellow bar, although the yellow bars are only visible for 'm' values 6 to 10, while the purple bars are visible for the same range but are not directly adjacent to the yellow bars due to the separate grouping for each 'm'. The bars are not sorted in any particular order beyond the categorical 'm' value. The diagram does not highlight any specific bars beyond the color distinction between the two sampling strategies.
